title: Wispr Flow alternatives for Mac in 2026, compared with real prices and privacy
metaTitle: Wispr Flow alternatives for Mac (with real prices)
description: Wispr Flow alternatives for Mac compared on real prices, offline use, privacy and platforms: Superwhisper, Aqua Voice, Willow Voice and Lazur.
secondaryKeywords: offline dictation mac alternative to wispr flow
intro: Superwhisper, Aqua Voice and Willow Voice are the closest Mac alternatives to Wispr Flow. All three are dictation apps. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates, so it fits a different job. Prices come from each company's own site, checked on 2026-11-07, and any price we could not confirm is marked as such.
tldr: Lowest price with a confirmed figure: Aqua Voice Pro at $10/month billed annually.
Offline dictation: Superwhisper with local models, and Willow Voice with its Offline Mode.
Dictation with Edit Mode and Deep Context: Aqua Voice, which has a free plan of 1,000 words.
Dictation plus help with what is on your screen: Lazur, a Mac-only voice assistant with a 3-day trial.

blocks.text: Who this comparison is for
You probably found Wispr Flow first. Maybe the monthly price stings. Maybe you need offline dictation, or an app that does more than type. This page covers four Mac apps that solve a similar problem.

Three of them are dictation apps like Wispr Flow: Superwhisper, Aqua Voice and Willow Voice. The fourth, Lazur, is a voice assistant that sees your screen and also dictates. That difference changes which app fits you, so it comes up again below.
Wispr Flow prices to beat

Wispr Flow's pricing page lists a Free plan at $0/mo. Pro costs $15/user/mo on monthly billing, or $12/user/mo on annual billing. The annual toggle is labeled 20% discount. Use those figures as the baseline for the rest of this page.

Wispr Flow also lists Growth and Enterprise plans. Growth is labeled "Our most popular plan." It shows $23/user/mo and $33/user/mo in the monthly view, and $18/user/mo and $26/user/mo in the annual view. The page does not say which figure is the crossed-out price, so check it on the page before you buy.

The Notetaker feature comes with full access through November 30 at no extra cost, according to the page. The page gives no year. After that, members would move to a limited plan. The page says the price will not automatically increase.
Superwhisper pricing: what you can confirm

Superwhisper's home page shows a Free plan at $0. The free plan includes voice-to-text in any app, 100+ languages and unlimited Whisper models. The Pro price is hard to read on the home page. Its /pricing address returned a 404 error when we checked on 2026-11-07. This page does not quote a Pro price it cannot confirm.

Third-party sites quote $8.49/month, $84.99/year and $249.99 for a lifetime license. Voibe, a competitor that sells its own dictation app, publishes those figures and says it checked them. We did not confirm them on Superwhisper's own site. Treat them as unverified until you see them there.
Offline dictation and privacy, app by app

Offline use is the main reason people move off a cloud app. Superwhisper is the clearest case. Its privacy policy says that when you use a local model, your audio and transcripts never leave your device. Its home page says Intel Macs work best with cloud models, because offline models run well only on Apple silicon.

Willow Voice has an Offline Mode that runs dictation on-device. Its Private Mode turns on automatically. Its help center says Willow does not retain dictated text or screen content in that mode. The optional Help Willow Improve setting is different. With it on, Willow collects your transcript text to improve accuracy and writing quality. No audio is collected.

Wispr Flow discards audio once it is transcribed, unless Dictation cloud storage is on. Turn that setting off and, the company says, nothing you say is used to train its models. Its pages list no offline mode, so plan on a connection for every dictation.

Aqua Voice is cloud-only in what we read. Its home page says Privacy Mode stores nothing on Aqua's servers, and Business plans include zero data retention. The home page text we read does not say whether data trains AI models. Ask Aqua directly before you send client material.

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur's product facts list no offline mode.
Certifications and what they actually cover

Wispr Flow's privacy page says it is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. It also offers HIPAA-ready dictation with a signed BAA on Growth and Enterprise. Accepting the BAA turns off Scratchpad and MCP connectors. If you handle patient records, read that section first.

Willow's home page says its Business plan adds an enforced privacy mode, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA. Its privacy policy, as we read it, does not mention SOC 2 or HIPAA. Ask Willow for the current report before you rely on the claim.

Aqua's SOC 2 Type II claim appears only in a competitor's review. We did not find it on Aqua's own pages. A certificate covers how a company runs its systems. It does not tell you how your audio is handled on the day you dictate. Read the data terms too.
Accuracy claims: read them as marketing

Aqua Voice's home page reports 97.4% key-term accuracy for its Avalon model, against 65.1% for Whisper Large v3. The test is called AISpeak-10. Aqua ran that benchmark itself, so treat it as a vendor result. We did not find an equivalent figure for the other apps on their pages.

blocks.title: Test it yourself
blocks.text: A vendor score can be accurate and still miss your jargon. Read one page of your own notes into each app. Count the words you had to fix. That count matters more than any benchmark.
Where each alternative is the better pick
Each of these apps beats the others on something. Here is where the others are better, stated plainly.

items: Superwhisper is better if local models and custom modes matter most. It also runs on Linux, which none of the other apps list.
Wispr Flow is better if you want one dictation app across Mac, Windows, iOS and Android, or a signed BAA for HIPAA-ready dictation.
Aqua Voice is better if you want to test a free plan of 1,000 words first, or if you want Edit Mode and Deep Context.
Willow Voice is better if you want an offline mode with Private Mode on by default, or a free plan with an unlimited weaker model.
Lazur is better if you want the app to answer questions about your screen, point at buttons and walk you through a new app.

blocks.text: One reviewer, Nick Lafferty, calls the cleanup Wispr Flow's biggest advantage over built-in dictation. The same reviewer writes that Flow sometimes cleans up a sentence in a way they would not. That is one opinion, so use it as a prompt for your own test.
A worked example: drafting by voice while you learn an app

Say you dictate a client memo for an hour each morning. Your problem is text, with good names and clean punctuation. Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, Aqua Voice or Willow Voice all fit that job. Pick by price, privacy and platform.

Now change the job. You need to change a privacy setting in an app you have never opened, and you do not want to hunt through menus. Lazur fits that job better. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask the question, and Lazur circles the button and labels it.

Lazur does not click the button for you. You click, and Lazur waits for each click. For the memo, the writing is still yours. Lazur helps you find the right place in the app, so you spend less time searching.
Mistakes people make when they switch dictation apps

items: Testing with one short sentence. Dictate a full page of your real work, with names and jargon, before you pay.
Ignoring the free limit. Aqua Voice's free plan stops at 1,000 words, so a test can end early.
Trusting the cleanup without reading it. Read the output once before you send it. The reviewer above says the cleanup sometimes changes a sentence they would not.
Comparing monthly prices only. Wispr's annual Pro is $12/user/mo against $15/user/mo monthly. Check the billing toggle on every site.
Assuming offline means private. Check the settings. Willow's Help Willow Improve setting collects transcript text when it is turned on.
Mixing up a dictation app with an assistant. Dictation writes your words. An assistant also points, explains and answers out loud.

blocks.text: How to test two apps in one afternoon

items: Start the free plan or trial. Lazur's 3-day Pro trial needs no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app.
Pick one page of real work. Use the same page in every app so the results match.
Dictate that page in each app. Note how long it takes, then count the words you fix. Log the results with the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker).
Turn off cloud storage where the app offers the setting. Wispr's privacy page says nothing you say is used to train its models once that setting is off.
Compare your own speed with the [typing speed test](/tools/typing-speed-test). A 2017 phone study measured 153 WPM for speech against 52 WPM for keyboard input, but your numbers matter more.

blocks.text: What to do next
Shortlist two apps from the list above. Run the test on your own work, not on a demo sentence. Then read the privacy page for the app you plan to keep.

If Lazur made your shortlist, start with the trial. You can [download Lazur](/download) or read the [Lazur pricing](/pricing) first. For a side-by-side view, read [Superwhisper vs Wispr Flow on Mac in 2026](/compare/superwhisper-vs-wispr-flow) or [Lazur vs Wispr Flow on Mac](/compare/lazur-vs-wispr-flow).

faq.question: What is the best free Wispr Flow alternative for Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's built-in Dictation is free and comes with macOS. Among the apps on this page, Superwhisper and Willow Voice both list a free plan. Aqua Voice's free plan covers 1,000 words. Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card.

faq.question: Is there a Wispr Flow alternative with a lifetime license?
faq.answer: Superwhisper's home page shows a lifetime option in its billing toggle. The price is not confirmed on the site, and its /pricing page returned a 404 error when we checked. A third-party site quotes $249.99 for lifetime. Check Superwhisper's own site before you rely on that number.

faq.question: Which alternative works offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Superwhisper runs local models that keep audio and transcripts on your device. Willow Voice has an Offline Mode that runs on-device. The Wispr Flow, Aqua Voice and Lazur pages we read do not list an offline mode. Lazur sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers to answer you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. If you need one app on both systems, Wispr Flow, Superwhisper or Aqua Voice list Windows support.

faq.question: Can Lazur replace Wispr Flow for dictation?
faq.answer: Lazur dictates too. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is unlimited on Pro and Power. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you, so it is an assistant first and a dictation tool second.

faq.question: What does Wispr Flow Pro cost?
faq.answer: Wispr Flow's pricing page lists Pro at $15/user/mo on monthly billing. On annual billing it is $12/user/mo, and the toggle is labeled 20% discount. The page also lists Growth and Enterprise plans, with Enterprise listed as Custom.

faq.question: Do these apps use what I say to train AI?
faq.answer: Wispr says nothing you say is used to train its models once Dictation cloud storage is off. Superwhisper's privacy policy says user data is not used to train AI models. Lazur says content is never used to train AI models. The Aqua home page text we read does not say. Check each privacy page before you dictate client or patient information.

verdict: Pick Superwhisper if local models and custom modes matter most. Pick Wispr Flow if you need one dictation app across Mac, Windows and phones, or a signed BAA. Pick Aqua Voice if you want to test a free plan first. Pick Willow Voice if you want an offline mode and a free plan. Pick Lazur if you want dictation plus help with what is on your screen.
